newsitem.title: USA: Tight hog supply forces cutbacks at U.S. packers.
newsitem.headline: Tight hog supply forces cutbacks at U.S. packers.

text.p: A tight supply of market-ready hogs has prompted several meat packers to cut pork production this month, the latest being IBP Inc which on Wednesday said it cut work hours four to eight hours a week this week and next.

"There are just not enough hogs out there," said Mark Klein, spokesman for Cargill Inc, the parent company of beef and pork processor Excel Corp. "We are continuing in a reduced mode that we have been in for several weeks."
Excel operates pork plants at Ottumwa, Iowa; Beardstown, Ill.; and Marshall, Mo. Klein said the company does not specify the extent of its production cutbacks.
IBP on Wednesday said "continued processing overcapacity and tight hog supplies" prompted the company to further reduce production at its seven pork plants.

A Smithfield Foods Inc spokeswoman said no changes in hog slaughter were planned at Smithfield Foods Inc plants, but she said company officials who could comment further were not available for comment.
Smithfield on Wednesday in a statement blamed its disappointing fourth quarter fresh meat results on other Midwest pork companies not cutting back production.
On May 5, a Smithfield official said slaughter was reduced at the company's two John Morrell and Co. plants, while reductions were limited at its two Virgina plants and the North Carolina plant.
Hormel Foods Corp on Thursday reported slightly higher second quarter earnings but added that high raw material costs should continue through its third quarter.

"The high costs which have had a severe impact on our operations for the better part of a year are now projected to continue at least throught the third quarter," said Hormel chairman and chief executive Joel Johnson, in a release. "The decline in hog supplies forced company plants to operate below optimum levels," Johnson said.
Officials at ConAgra Inc, Thorn Apple Valley and Farmland Industries were unavailable for comment Thursday, but earlier this month, ConAgra and Farmland said they had reduced hog slaughter.
